title: Adaptive client graceful degradation spec
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview
--------
This spec defines a standardized, API-driven approach for client-side graceful degradation when Redwood services (edge-proxy, redwood-api-gateway, model-router, inference-runtime) signal reduced capacity, elevated latency, or partial feature removal. The goal is to keep downstream applications available with predictable quality and cost characteristics, reduce cascading failures, and enable coordinated rollouts for degraded modes.

Scope
-----
Applies to: public SDKs (JS, Python, Go), internal service-to-service clients, third-party customers integrating with Redwood API.
Not in scope: human-facing UI presentation rules (product teams control UX).

Principles
----------
- Deterministic: clients must follow a machine-readable contract (headers + payload hints).
- Observable: degradation decisions must emit telemetry (events, tags, traces).
- Reversible: services must provide clear 'restore' signals and TTLs for hints.
- Minimal surface: default-safe behaviors must be implemented in SDKs so integrators do not need bespoke logic.

Signals and Contract
--------------------
Runtime components may attach hints to responses or push via a control channel. Primary mechanisms:
1) HTTP response headers from redwood-api-gateway / edge-proxy
   - X-Redwood-Degrade: none | latency | cost | fidelity | regional
   - X-Redwood-Degrade-Variant: low_fidelity | short_context | cached | fallback_model:v2
   - X-Redwood-Degrade-Until: 2026-12-10T15:36:00Z (ISO-8601 TTL)
   - X-Redwood-Rationale: capacity | thermal | deployment | maintenance
2) Structured JSON field in streaming/event envelopes (when streaming endpoints are used)
   - {"degrade":{"mode":"fidelity","variant":"short_context","ttl":"PT5M"}}
3) Push control channel (internal): service-mesh config updates and feature-flagging endpoint (for private deployments)

Client behavior matrix (required default SDK behavior)
---------------------------------------------------
- X-Redwood-Degrade: none -> normal processing.
- latency -> if p95 backend latency > configured threshold, clients should:
  1) enable speculative early-exit (if available) to return partial tokens up to quality threshold.
  2) reduce concurrent streaming buffer (to avoid head-of-line blocking).
- cost -> prefer cached responses, reduce max_tokens by 30%, and set generation_temperature to 0.2 (if applicable).
- fidelity -> apply variant mapping: 
  - low_fidelity: use model variants marked as compatible in capability manifest (see Model Variant Table).
  - short_context: trim oldest user-turns until request payload < 1024 tokens.
- regional -> prefer fallback-region endpoints (fall back to edge-proxy region mapping).

Rules and thresholds (default SDK config)
---------------------------------------
- Default client thresholds (can be overridden by client config):
  - latency-warning-threshold: p95 >= 300ms -> treat as latency degrade hint after 3 consecutive responses.
  - latency-critical-threshold: p99 >= 800ms -> escalate: apply 'latency' degrade mode immediately.
  - error-rate-threshold: 5% 4xx/5xx in 60s sliding window -> treat as cost/degradation depending on error codes.
  - ttl-fallback-max: 1h (SDK will not obey degrade hints with TTLs > 1h without explicit opt-in).

Model Variant Table (example)
-----------------------------
| Variant ID       | Compatible APIs       | Expected latency uplift | Quality impact | Owner |
|------------------|----------------------|-------------------------|----------------|-------|
| fallback-sm-1    | text.generate, chat  | 0.6x latency             | -10% accuracy  | runtime-team |
| quantized-low-2  | embeddings, rerank   | 0.4x latency             | -4% accuracy   | runtime-team |

Clients must consult the model capability manifest endpoint (/v1/models/{id}/manifest) to validate variant compatibility before switching. If incompatibility is detected, fallback to cached or short-context behavior.

Telemetry and Observability
---------------------------
Clients and services MUST emit the following fields for every degradation event:
- event_type: degrade_hint_received | degrade_action_taken | degrade_restored
- origin: redwood-api-gateway | edge-proxy | model-router | inference-runtime
- degrade_mode: none | latency | cost | fidelity | regional
- variant_applied: (string) or 'none'
- ttl_seconds: (int) or 0
- client_id / sdk_version / host_service
- trace_id / request_id

Implementations: SDKs should add an instrumented event to the telemetry pipeline and increment a counter metric: client.degrade_actions_total{mode,variant}. Alerting rules in dashboards:
- Increase in degrade_action_taken > 5% of traffic in 5m -> P1 for runtime on-call.

Contract examples
-----------------
Header example (HTTP):
X-Redwood-Degrade: fidelity
X-Redwood-Degrade-Variant: low_fidelity
X-Redwood-Degrade-Until: 2026-12-10T15:36:00Z

Streaming envelope example (JSON snippet):
{"event":"hint","degrade":{"mode":"cost","variant":"cached","ttl":"PT2M","reason":"capacity"}}

SDK pseudocode (JS)
-------------------
// client-level handler registered by default in SDK
async function handleResponseHints(resp) {
  const mode = resp.headers.get('x-redwood-degrade');
  if (!mode || mode === 'none') return;
  const variant = resp.headers.get('x-redwood-degrade-variant') || 'none';
  const until = resp.headers.get('x-redwood-degrade-until');
  emitTelemetry('degrade_hint_received', {mode, variant, until});
  switch (mode) {
    case 'fidelity': applyFidelityFallback(variant, until); break;
    case 'latency': enableEarlyExitUntil(until); break;
    case 'cost': reduceTokensAndTemperature(); break;
    case 'regional': switchRegionFallback(); break;
  }
  emitTelemetry('degrade_action_taken', {mode, variant});
}

Operational runbook (on-call)
-----------------------------
1) Pager fires if degrade_action_taken > 5% of requests in 5m.
2) Check dashboards: edge-proxy latency, model-router queue length, inference-runtime GPU saturation.
3) If cause == thermal or GPU preemption -> follow GPU-fleet maintenance playbook (eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity).
4) If cause == deployment -> rollback canary via rollout service: /internal/rollouts -> rollback to previous stable revision.
5) If cause == config (misapplied feature flag) -> disable flag and run synthetic requests to validate restore.
6) Communicate to product owners and customers via status page if degradation predicted > 30m.

Rollout and SDK adoption plan
-----------------------------
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): SDK maintainers implement header parsing and default behaviors in JS/Python/Go; feature flag to opt-out for customers.
- Phase 1 (1 month): Gradual enablement for 20% of traffic for internal services; collect metrics.
- Phase 2 (3 months): Make default for all public SDKs; update docs and notify customers via changelog.

Config table (defaults and allowed ranges)
----------------------------------------
| config_key                      | default         | allowed range / notes |
|---------------------------------|-----------------|------------------------|
| latency_warning_threshold_ms    | 300             | 100–2000              |
| latency_critical_threshold_ms   | 800             | 300–5000              |
| error_rate_window_seconds       | 60              | 30–300                |
| error_rate_threshold_pct        | 5               | 1–20                 |
| ttl_fallback_max_seconds        | 3600            | 0–86400              |

Security and privacy considerations
----------------------------------
- Degradation headers MUST NOT carry user PII. X-Redwood-Rationale may contain short non-PII tags only.
- For private deployments, control-channel messages must be signed; SDKs must verify signature if control-channel is used.

Testing and verification
------------------------
- Unit tests: SDKs must include mocked response headers and assert expected behavior paths.
- Integration tests: synthetic workload that simulates p95/p99 latency spikes and verifies telemetry counters and that degradation restores after TTL expiry.
- Chaos test: inject degrade hints via feature flagging service to validate end-to-end behavior across client libraries.

Ownership and maintenance
-------------------------
- Owner: Runtime Reliability (eng-serving-runtime) – primary contact: runtime-reliability@redwood.com
- SDK implementations: eng-developer-experience team
- Observability and alerts: eng-platform dashboards team

Open questions / future work
--------------------------
- Should degrade hints be prioritized by customer tier (e.g., Dedicated customers should get fewer fidelity fallbacks)?
- Can we extend this contract to include probabilistic fallback rates for A/B-style degradation?
- Evaluate a signed, push-based degrade byte stream for on-prem customers behind private control planes.

Appendix: quick CLI examples
---------------------------
- Inspect header for a request (curl):
curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat 
# look for X-Redwood-Degrade* headers

- Emit a synthetic degrade hint for testing (internal tool):
# internal-only tool: /internal/test-degrade --mode fidelity --variant low_fidelity --ttl PT1M --target service=model-router

References
----------
- Model capability manifest: /v1/models/{id}/manifest
- Rollout service: /internal/rollouts
- GPU fleet playbooks: /confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/gpu-maintenance-orchestration-and-tenant-fairness-policy-2026
